android.desc:
Guardia del Campo is the daily phytosanitary bulletin for those who work the land in Sannio.

Every morning, the app tells you what's happening in your field and what to do: disease risks, weather alerts, treatment windows, and operational advice—all tailored to the crops and varieties of the area.

WHAT THE APP DOES

🍇 Vineyard
Risks for downy mildew, powdery mildew, botrytis, and grape vine moth. Phenology for Aglianico, Falanghina, Merlot, and Syrah with a countdown to bud break. Copper treatment windows with wind and rain forecasts.

🫒 Olive Grove
Risks for olive fly, peacock eye, and scab. Phenology for Ortice, Racioppella, Ortolana, and Ravece—the varieties of Sannio. Specific warnings for the susceptibility of each cultivar.

🥬 Vegetable Garden
Seasonal calendar: what to plant this month, frost protection, safe planting windows.

🌤 Weather and Environmental Risks
Frost, hail, drought, fires, floods, strong winds, Saharan dust—all in one bulletin with 3-, 7-, and 14-day forecasts.

FIELD REPORTS
The most important part. See something in the field? A leaf spot, hail damage, an early pest? Report it in one minute. Each report improves the accuracy of the alerts for all farmers in the area. Anonymous, no registration required.

WHY IT'S DIFFERENT
- Daily bulletin with concrete actions, not just data
- Calibrated for the local Sannio varieties (not generic)
- 7- and 14-day forecasts with artificial intelligence models
- Explanations: for each risk, the app tells you WHY it is high or low
- Push notifications only when you need to take action (frost, hail, pests)
- Free, no ads, no registration

DATA AND SOURCES
The data comes from NASA POWER, Open-Meteo, ECMWF, and local weather stations. The risk models are based on agronomic literature and calibrated for the Sannio climate (428 m, hilly Mediterranean).

WHO WE ARE
Guardia del Campo was born from the guardia.sann.io platform, a civic project for the Sannio region. No personal data is collected, no advertising, and the code is based on open data.

The more people report, the better the system works. Sannio has 10,000 hectares of vineyards and nearly 8,000 winemakers—if even just a few of them start reporting what they see, everyone will benefit.

quotes.text:
I'm a Senior Engineer in Berlin. My hometown is Guardia Sanframondi — a hilltop village of ~5,000 people in Southern Italy's Sannio wine region. Local farmers grow heritage grapes (Falanghina, Aglianico) and olive cultivars that have been here for centuries.

One evening I was looking at Copernicus satellite data and thought: could I turn NDVI imagery and weather data into something useful for the farmers I grew up with? That turned into months of evenings and weekends.

What it does: Guardia del Campo combines satellite imagery (Sentinel-2 NDVI, soil moisture), weather data (Open-Meteo, ARPA Campania), and ML models trained on local varieties to produce daily risk forecasts for downy mildew, powdery mildew, olive fly, frost, and heat stress. Every morning, a Gemini AI brief tells farmers what to do — in plain Italian. No "probability coefficient." Just: "humidity is high, check the vines for peronospora today."

The part I'm most proud of: anonymous crowdsourced reporting. A farmer spots disease, taps three buttons, every grower within 10km gets an alert. No account, no login, no personal data. Works offline, syncs when connectivity returns.
Stack: Next.js + Vercel (dashboard + cron jobs for ML pipeline), Supabase (Postgres + Edge Functions), Python/scikit-learn (daily-retrained SGD models), Gemini API (Italian agronomic briefs), Capacitor (wraps the web app as native Android — same codebase, Play Store, native push). Capacitor over React Native because the entire product …
